{"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol-required files exactly: requirements.txt, Main.py, tests/test_main.py. Keep Main.py a thin, non-interactive bootstrap that constructs a playlist, a deterministic ManualClock, and a Player, performs a few scripted operations, and exits. Place reusable modules in a lowercase snake_case package named video_player. Separate pure domain logic (media metadata, playlist rules, playback state transitions, seeking, volume/mute) from environment/runtime concerns. Provide a headless, deterministic clock abstraction with a tick-driven model: the Player subscribes to a provided clock and advances only on ticks. Tests drive time deterministically by calling ManualClock.tick(...) directly; no GUI, audio, filesystem, or network. Use only pytest as an external dependency. tests execute deterministically via ManualClock without I/O, GUI, audio, filesystem, or network"},"Full API spec":"Public API and import rules

Package: video_player
- video_player.__init__ re-exports: ValidationError, StateError, NotFoundError; Media; ManualClock; Playlist; Player; PlaybackState.
- Import graph must be acyclic: errors -> media -> playlist -> player; clock is orthogonal and imported by player only; tests and Main.py import from video_player or submodules without creating cycles.

Exceptions (video_player.errors)
- class ValidationError(Exception): raised for invalid inputs and configuration.
- class StateError(ValidationError): raised for invalid state transitions (e.g., play with empty playlist).
- class NotFoundError(ValidationError): raised when addressing non-existent playlist indices/items.

Entity: Media (video_player.media)
- class Media:
  - __init__(self, id: str, title: str, duration_seconds: float, metadata: Optional[dict] = None)
    - id: non-empty str
    - title: non-empty str
    - duration_seconds: float > 0
    - metadata: optional dict; stored as a shallow copy; object is immutable after construction (no setters; attributes may be read-only via properties or by convention).
  - Attributes (public, read-only): id, title, duration_seconds, metadata (a shallow-copied dict or {})
  - Errors: ValidationError for invalid field types/values.

Clock: ManualClock (video_player.clock)
- class ManualClock:
  - now(self) -> float: returns accumulated clock time in seconds.
  - add_tick_listener(self, fn: Callable[[float], None]) -> None: registers a listener to receive tick deltas; idempotent add allowed; listener called synchronously on tick in registration order.
  - remove_tick_listener(self, fn) -> None: unregisters a previously added listener; no-op if not present.
  - tick(self, delta_seconds: float) -> None: advances clock by delta_seconds (> 0) and synchronously notifies listeners via fn(delta_seconds). Raises ValidationError if delta_seconds <= 0.

Playlist (video_player.playlist)
- class Playlist:
  - __init__(self, items: list[Media]): stores an immutable snapshot list of Media; initial _current_index is 0 if non-empty else None.
  - is_empty(self) -> bool: True if no items.
  - size(self) -> int: number of items.
  - current(self) -> Media | None: current Media if selected else None.
  - select(self, index: int) -> Media: selects and returns item at index; raises NotFoundError for out-of-range; sets current index to index.
  - next(self) -> Media | None: if empty, return None; if at last item, keep last and return None; otherwise advance index by 1 and return the new current item.
  - previous(self) -> Media | None: if empty, return None; if at first item, keep first and return None; otherwise decrement index by 1 and return the new current item.
  - Invariants: indices are 0-based; navigation does not wrap; selection maintains bounds.

PlaybackState (video_player.player)
- enum-like class PlaybackState with three members: STOPPED, PLAYING, PAUSED. Comparable by identity or value; string reprs stable.

Player (video_player.player)
- class Player:
  - __init__(self, playlist: Playlist, clock: ManualClock): subscribes an internal _on_tick listener to clock; initializes state STOPPED, position 0.0, volume 1.0, muted False. If playlist not empty, current selection is as in Playlist (index 0 by default).
  - state(self) -> PlaybackState: returns current playback state.
  - current_media(self) -> Media | None: returns playlist.current().
  - position_seconds(self) -> float: current position within current media in seconds; 0.0 when no selection.
  - duration_seconds(self) -> float: duration of current media in seconds; 0.0 when no selection.
  - play(self) -> None: transitions to PLAYING if a media is selected; if playlist is empty, raises StateError; if at end (position >= duration), resets to 0.0 before playing.
  - pause(self) -> None: transitions to PAUSED from PLAYING; no-op if already PAUSED or STOPPED (remains STOPPED).
  - stop(self) -> None: transitions to STOPPED and resets position to 0.0.
  - seek(self, seconds: float) -> float: clamps seconds to [0.0, duration_seconds()] and sets position; returns the effective position. If no media selected, returns 0.0 and leaves state STOPPED. Raises ValidationError for NaN or negative infinite values; finite negatives clamp to 0.0.
  - set_volume(self, v: float) -> float: sets volume to clamp(v, 0.0, 1.0); returns effective volume.
  - get_volume(self) -> float: returns current volume (0.0..1.0), independent of muted flag.
  - mute(self) -> None: sets muted True.
  - unmute(self) -> None: sets muted False.
  - toggle_mute(self) -> bool: flips muted and returns new muted state.
  - effective_volume(self) -> float: returns 0.0 if muted else get_volume().
  - next_media(self) -> Media | None: requests playlist.next(); if a next item exists, resets position to 0.0 and sets state to STOPPED; returns the Media or None if at end.
  - previous_media(self) -> Media | None: requests playlist.previous(); if a previous item exists, resets position to 0.0 and sets state to STOPPED; returns the Media or None if at start.
  - select_index(self, i: int) -> Media: delegates to playlist.select(i); resets position to 0.0 and sets state to STOPPED; returns selected Media.
  - _on_tick(self, delta: float) -> None: internal; invoked by ManualClock ticks; advances position only when state is PLAYING and a current media exists; clamps at duration and transitions to STOPPED when reaching or exceeding end, leaving position at exact duration.
  - _reset_position(self) -> None: internal; sets position to 0.0.

Semantics
- Deterministic, headless, tick-driven: Player time advances only via ManualClock.tick calls; no wall-clock usage. End-of-media behavior: when position + delta >= duration, set position to duration and set state to STOPPED.
- No I/O, no GUI/audio/network/filesystem side effects anywhere in core modules.

__init__ exports (video_player.__init__)
- from .errors import ValidationError, StateError, NotFoundError
- from .media import Media
- from .clock import ManualClock
- from .playlist import Playlist
- from .player import Player, PlaybackState

Import constraints
- errors is leaf; media imports errors; playlist imports media and errors; player imports errors, media, playlist, and clock; clock imports nothing from domain; __init__ re-exports only.

Runtime entry (Main.py)
- Constructs a small list of Media, a Playlist, a ManualClock, and a Player. Demonstrates play/pause/seek/next and ticks deterministically, then exits without interaction or I/O.","Shared Knowledge":"The project provides a headless, deterministic video player domain. Core modules live under video_player/*.py and do not touch environment concerns. ManualClock provides a tick-driven time source; Player subscribes to it and advances only on ticks. The import graph is acyclic: errors -> media -> playlist -> player, with clock orthogonal and used only by player. The package initializer re-exports the public API. Main.py is a thin bootstrap demo. tests/test_main.py imports video_player and exercises deterministic behaviors: clock-driven progression, seek clamping, volume/mute, and playlist navigation. No GUI, audio, filesystem, or network are used.","Execution Protocol":"Run tests with: python -m pytest -q. Exactly one protocol-level test file exists: tests/test_main.py. The runtime entrypoint is Main.py, which is non-interactive and purely demonstrative. The test drives time deterministically by calling ManualClock.tick(...). No additional files alter protocol-required files.","Anything UNCLEAR":""}
